response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-20
CLINICAL INDICATION: Known lung nodule under surveillance. Admitted with fever. Portable film. Has the nodule changed?
ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. S. Whitfield (synthetic), medical oncology
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-08-21
TECHNIQUE: Current AP. Prior PA. Projection differs from the prior. Current film is also underexposed with a likely lordotic beam angle. Both films are mildly rotated. Comparability is limited (both blind reads agree).

LOOK AT FIRST:
- None. No finding is flagged time-sensitive. Triage urgency is high and the case needs radiologist review. On-call page is not triggered.

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea is poorly seen through the underexposed upper mediastinum, with no gross displacement. Hazy, ill-defined opacity in the right lower zone reaches the lower right mid zone on the current film. It obscures the right heart border and medial right hemidiaphragm, with apparent right basal volume loss. It is present on both studies and is indeterminate for change (both reads agreed). Coarse linear and reticular markings in the left mid and lower zones on both studies, similar distribution, no new confluent opacity in the left lung (seen on one of two reads). Vascular markings reach the chest wall on both sides, with no pleural line. Small nodules and fine interstitial change cannot be excluded on the underexposed current film.
- Mediastinum / hila: Aortic knuckle is prominent with an unfolded contour on both studies. The upper mediastinum looks wider on the AP current film. This is expected with AP projection and is not called as a change. This finding is indeterminate and the two reads disagreed (one stable, one indeterminate). The right hilum and infrahilar region are prominent and continuous with the right lower zone opacity on both studies, so a hilar lesion cannot be separated from vessels or adjacent lung opacity. This is indeterminate and was raised by one of two reads. The left hilum is not clearly enlarged.
- Pleura: Lateral right costophrenic sulcus is aerated and pointed, while the medial right base is opaque. Subpulmonic or layering fluid is not excluded. Left costophrenic angle is sharp. No pneumothorax. Right hemidiaphragm contour is high and indistinct medially on both studies, with an aerated lateral sulcus. Interval change is indeterminate and the two reads disagreed (one indeterminate, one stable). Left dome is sharp. No free gas is identified, but the upper abdomen is underexposed on the current film.
- Heart: Cardiac silhouette appears prominent on the PA prior and enlarged on the AP current. AP projection magnifies the heart, and the right heart border is obscured on both films. Indeterminate, not comparable (both reads agreed).
- Bones / soft tissue: No displaced rib fracture or gross destructive bone lesion, but bone detail is limited by underexposure. Chest wall soft tissue is prominent. No soft tissue gas. No lines, tubes, pacemaker or other internal device identified, and no new device since the prior.

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: No change can be called. The right lower zone opacity appears more extensive on the current film, but this may be explained by AP projection, underexposure and overlying soft tissue, so size and density change are not comparable. Heart size, mediastinal width, hilar size, pleural fluid and right hemidiaphragm height cannot be compared across PA and AP projections.
- Unchanged: The right lower zone opacity is present in the same location on both films, with the same loss of the right heart border and medial right hemidiaphragm. Left mid and lower zone linear and reticular markings have a similar distribution (density not compared because of the exposure difference; one of two reads). Aortic knuckle has the same shape and position on both films, but the reads disagreed on this item. No new device.

RECIST 1.1: not computed on radiographs

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Has the right lower zone opacity changed in size or density since the prior? | Reason: Prior is PA and current is AP and underexposed. Projection and exposure differences can make a basal opacity look larger or denser. | Recommend: CT chest, or repeat PA and lateral when the patient is able.
- Is there a right pleural effusion, including a subpulmonic component, and has it changed? | Reason: The high, indistinct right basal contour with an aerated lateral sulcus could reflect subpulmonic fluid, an elevated hemidiaphragm, or basal volume loss. A frontal film alone cannot separate these, and patient position on the current AP is not shown. | Recommend: Lateral or right lateral decubitus view, ultrasound of the right base, or CT chest.
- Is there a right hilar or infrahilar mass or adenopathy underlying the right basal opacity and volume loss? | Reason: The right hilum merges with the adjacent opacity on both films. Mild rotation and the AP projection make hilar size unreliable. | Recommend: CT chest, with contrast if appropriate.
- Has heart size changed? | Reason: AP projection magnifies the heart, and cardiothoracic ratio is valid on PA films only. The right heart border is also obscured on both studies. | Recommend: Repeat PA film when the patient is able, or echocardiography if clinically relevant.
- Is the right hemidiaphragm truly elevated, or is the contour formed by subpulmonic fluid or a process below the diaphragm? | Reason: The true diaphragm is not separately visible on a frontal film. The lordotic AP beam angle on the current film also alters the apparent dome height. | Recommend: Ultrasound of the right upper quadrant and right base, or CT covering the chest and upper abdomen.
- Are there small nodules or fine interstitial changes in either lung on the current study? | Reason: The current film is underexposed with heavy soft tissue overlap, and the clavicles project over the apices. Small nodules cannot be confirmed or excluded. | Recommend: CT chest, or repeat PA and lateral with adequate exposure.
- Has the heart enlarged since the prior? | Reason: Prior is PA and current is AP. AP projection magnifies the heart, and the right heart border is obscured on both films. | Recommend: Repeat PA and lateral when the patient is able, or CT chest.
- Has the right lower zone opacity grown, shrunk, or stayed the same? | Reason: Projection differs (PA then AP) and the current film is underpenetrated. Size and density change cannot be reported across these differences. | Recommend: Repeat PA and lateral with good inspiration, or CT chest.
- Is the high right hemidiaphragm contour a truly elevated diaphragm, a subpulmonic effusion, or lower lobe volume loss? | Reason: A frontal film alone cannot separate these. Patient position on the current AP film is unknown, and fluid layers out when supine. | Recommend: Lateral and right lateral decubitus views, ultrasound of the right base, or CT chest.
- Is the upper mediastinum truly wider on the current study? | Reason: AP projection, possible mild rotation, and underexposure each widen or blur the mediastinal contour. | Recommend: Repeat PA film, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.
- Are there small lung nodules or a hilar abnormality on the current study? | Reason: The current film is underpenetrated and low in contrast, with overlying soft tissue shadows. Small nodules and hilar detail cannot be assessed, and the right hilum is partly obscured by adjacent opacity on both studies. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with windowing; CT chest if a nodule or hilar lesion needs to be excluded.
- Is there a retrocardiac opacity? | Reason: Vertebrae are not visible behind the heart on the current film, and a frontal view alone cannot clear this area. | Recommend: Lateral view or CT chest.

IMPRESSION:
1. Hazy, ill-defined right lower zone opacity with apparent right basal volume loss, present on both studies (F1). Indeterminate for change: both reads agreed. Size and density cannot be compared because the prior is PA and the current is an underexposed AP. A new process within it cannot be confirmed or excluded.
2. Right hilar and infrahilar prominence continuous with the right lower zone opacity on both studies (F4). Indeterminate, with no call on size or change. A hilar lesion cannot be separated from vessels or adjacent opacity. Raised by one of two reads.
3. High right hemidiaphragm contour, indistinct medially, on both studies (F2). Indeterminate, and the two reads disagreed (one indeterminate, one stable). Subpulmonic fluid, true elevation and basal volume loss cannot be separated on frontal films.
4. Cardiac silhouette appears prominent on the PA prior and enlarged on the AP current (F3). Indeterminate and not comparable across projections. Both reads agreed.
5. Prominent aortic knuckle on both studies, with an upper mediastinum that looks wider on the AP current film (F5). Indeterminate, and the two reads disagreed (one stable, one indeterminate). Widening is not called as a change.
6. Coarse linear and reticular markings in the left mid and lower zones, similar distribution on both studies (F6). Stable by one of two reads. Density not compared.
7. Indication question: no discrete nodule can be identified and matched on both films, so change in the surveillance nodule cannot be judged from these images. The prior report mentions a nodular opacity (no side or zone) and a small pleural effusion (no side). Neither is confirmed on the images and neither has been adopted as a finding. Small nodules cannot be excluded on the underexposed current film.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- CT chest, with contrast if appropriate, to address the right lower zone opacity, right hilum, pleura and nodule surveillance. The input gives no interval, so timing is for the resident and attending to set. Alternatively, repeat PA and lateral chest radiograph with adequate exposure when the patient is able.
- Lateral or right lateral decubitus view, or ultrasound of the right base and right upper quadrant, for the right basal contour and possible subpulmonic fluid, if CT is not performed.
- Repeat PA film when the patient is able for heart size and mediastinal width, or echocardiography if clinically relevant.
- Review the source images in PACS with windowing.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
